sun.upright:
An Aries Sun tends to measure courage by speed. Cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, you're proudest of the version of yourself that moved first, before anyone else had worked out whether it was safe. Strength is fire as well. Leo sits four signs from Aries, a trine, so the card and your Sun get on without trying, and a same-element draw like this turns up whatever's already there. That means the confidence and the warmth, and it also means the appetite for a fight.

The catch is that the card's courage isn't the Aries kind. Yours goes in first and fast. Hers holds still while something big and dangerous calms down under her hands, with nothing to win and nobody keeping score. The Emperor is Aries's own card, and he's in charge because he says so, sitting on a stone throne with rams carved into it. Strength is in charge without saying anything at all. Most Aries Suns I've read for are stronger than the fights they pick, and this card knows it. You'll probably feel an itch about that. Something in your day will look like a challenge, you'll want to go straight at it, and the card is asking whether you need to.

At work it shows in the meeting where someone's wrong and you know it, and letting them finish would cost you nothing. At home it's the argument you're winning on volume. With your body it's training hard because you're angry, which feels good and leaves you sore in all the wrong places. Next time you're sure you're right, say it once, at an ordinary volume, and then stop talking.
sun.reversed:
With Strength upside down, an Aries Sun can start treating every difference of opinion as a contest to be won by teatime. Mars already runs hot in you, and the reversed card takes the patience away, so you push where waiting would have got you the same result a week later, and the pushing feels like proof you're strong. There's a quieter version too. Someone knocks your confidence and you go sharp and prickly, picking at small things because the big thing hurt.

At work you'll see it as steamrolling, deciding for a team that wanted a say. At home it's the standoff that started over whose turn it was to empty the dishwasher and has lasted three days, because backing down feels like losing. Your body keeps a record, the tight jaw, the sleep that never goes deep. Pick the argument you care least about and concede it out loud, and notice how little that costs you.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon feels things before it's decided to. Anger arrives in half a second, so does wanting, so does hurt, and the first thing you want to do with any of it is act. Mars rules Aries, so this is a Moon that's quick to defend itself and usually just as quick to get over it. Strength drawn for your tides shares your element and sits a trine away, which is probably why it lands gently. It's like having someone stand next to you who's plainly on your side.

What the card gives an Aries Moon is a gap. It's small, a breath or two between the flare and whatever you'd normally do next, and inside that gap you get a choice. You'll still feel the whole thing. Fire meeting fire doesn't cool anything down, if anything the feelings run bigger than usual, and you're allowed all of them. The skill is holding them for a second the way you'd hold a hot pan, firmly, without dropping it or throwing it. To be honest it's a skill most Aries Moons learn late, and usually after a few doors have been slammed.

With a partner it shows in the message you type fast and would regret by lunch. With family, it's the parent or sibling who still knows exactly which button to press. At night it's going to bed buzzing from something that happened at four o'clock. When you feel it rise, put your hands flat on the table and leave them there until the other person has finished talking.
moon.reversed:
Take away the gap and an Aries Moon is acting before the feeling's even finished arriving. The door, the message, the thing said in front of other people that you'll be apologising for on Thursday. For this Moon the speed is what does the damage. Sometimes it turns round and the anger points inward, a cross, restless feeling about not coping better, which is a miserable place for a Moon that likes to get things out of its system.

It comes out at home first, with whoever happens to be nearest. It comes out in the body as a kind of permanent readiness, appetite off, sleep short, shoulders never quite coming down. Gritting your teeth only adds more force to a system that's already got plenty. Go and do something hard and physical, a fast walk or a swim, and answer the thing that set you off once your breathing's back to normal.

rising.upright:
Aries rising comes through a door as if someone's timing it. Mars rules your chart, and people meeting you usually get somebody direct and quick, a bit of a challenge, the one who'll say the first thing and mean it. Strength on your mask barely slows that down. Leo and Aries are both fire and they sit a trine apart, so the card slides straight into your style and adds warmth to it. Strangers still get the drive, along with a sense that you aren't going to use it on them.

That's a bigger change than it sounds. A lot of Aries rising people get read as competitive before they've done anything, and some of them get tired of it, because it isn't what they meant. With this card the heat reads as confidence, and confident people are far easier to be around than people who look like they're about to test you. The risk with fire on fire is overdoing it. You can come on so strong that gentler people brace before you've said hello, and you won't notice, because from the inside it just feels friendly.

It helps in job interviews, where you're likely to come across as someone who can lead without making a fuss. It helps on first dates, and in any room where you don't know a soul. With a new team or new neighbours, the first week is when they decide about you. In the next room full of strangers, find the person who looks least comfortable and go and talk to them first.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on an Aries Ascendant, the warmth drops out and the push stays. People meet someone who seems ready for an argument nobody's started, quick to interrupt, a little too keen to show they won't be pushed around. Or the confidence wobbles and you cover it with sharpness, so a harmless question gets answered as though it were an attack, and the person who asked it goes quiet.

You'll notice it in first meetings that should have gone well and ended a bit cool, and in the way strangers either back off or push back harder. Mars is your chart ruler and it hates feeling cornered, even by a raised eyebrow. On a date it can look like competing with the person you're meant to be getting to know. Before you go into the next room that matters, take one slow breath at the door and walk in a step slower than you'd like.

sun.upright:
Two fixed signs meet here, and neither is famous for moving. A Taurus Sun is fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and you build yourself slowly out of things that last, the savings, the skill, the home, the reputation for not being rattled. Strength belongs to Leo, fixed fire, and Leo squares Taurus from three signs away. Squares are friction that makes you do something. Fire and earth have no natural bond in either direction, so this card and your Sun need an introduction, and it'll have a bit of grit in it.

Your strength is staying put. You can outlast nearly anyone, and there's real pride in that. The card's strength is warmer and it moves. The woman on it is doing something, gently, with her hands, in a situation where you'd more likely sit tight and wait for it to pass. So the question this draw raises is whether the thing you've refused to budge on is strength, or just the habit of not budging. Taurus Suns usually know the answer and don't much like it. Leo's pride and Taurus's stubbornness are hard to tell apart from outside, which is part of why the square stings. The Hierophant is your sign's own card, the way things have always been done, and Strength is asking you to put some heart back into the old way or let it go.

At work this looks like the process you defend because it's yours. With money it's the purchase you won't make even though it would make your life easier. In a long relationship it's the standoff you're both too proud to end. Be the first to bend on something small, and say something kind while you do it.
sun.reversed:
When Strength reverses for a Taurus Sun, steady turns into stuck. What you're calling patience is closer to refusing, and the square between the card and your sign grinds where it could have warmed, so every nudge from outside makes you plant your feet deeper. There's usually fear under it, the fixed-earth kind that goes quiet and heavy and holds on to what it's got, because letting go of anything feels like the first step to losing everything.

At work it's the small thing you'll go to war over. With money it's a grip that's tighter than the numbers need. In the body it sits in the neck and jaw, and sometimes in appetite, eating for comfort and then feeling slow. Venus rules Taurus and is much happier when things feel generous. Choose one thing you've been immovable about, change it by a small amount, and see what actually happens.

moon.upright:
Some feelings take months to arrive in a Taurus Moon, and months to leave. You settle through the body, food, sleep, a hot shower, the same chair every evening, and when something upsets you the first thing you reach for is comfort, which usually works. Venus rules Taurus, so pleasure genuinely calms you. Strength squares your Moon, two fixed signs pressing on each other, and fire and earth need introducing before they'll cooperate, so this card leans on your comfort a little.

What it leans on is the waiting. A Taurus Moon's way with a hard feeling is to sit it out somewhere soft until it passes, and plenty of them do pass. The ones that don't tend to set. A remark from a friend, a thing your partner said on holiday, sits in you for months, quiet and heavy, and you'd honestly prefer not to bring it up, because bringing it up would change things and change is the feeling you like least. Strength asks you to deal with a feeling while it's still warm and small enough to handle. That's uncomfortable for a fixed Moon. It's also where most of your resentment comes from, so the discomfort is worth it.

In the body it can show as evening snacking that isn't really about hunger, and sleep that's heavy without being restful. At home it's the grudge you're sitting on with a partner or housemate. With family it's the old argument everyone has agreed not to mention. When something annoys you, say so the same day, in one plain sentence, before you've had a chance to get comfortable with it.
moon.reversed:
A Taurus Moon with this card reversed goes very still. Something's upset you and the response is to get comfortable and stay comfortable, a long nap on a Saturday, bread and butter at eleven at night, a weekend in trackpants with the curtains half shut. Each one is harmless. Together they're a very good way of not feeling something. The fixed square makes it stubborn, and the more anyone nudges you, the more firmly you settle.

It usually comes out at home, where a resentment that's been sitting for months turns up in a flat voice about the dishes. It comes out in the body as heaviness and a sluggish gut. A partner may say you've gone far away while sitting right beside them. Say one thing you've been swallowing out loud, even if it's only to yourself in the car. Then tell the person it concerns, gently, somewhere you both feel comfortable.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising gives people calm on first meeting. Venus rules your chart, so you usually come across as pleasant, unhurried and nicely put together, someone it's easy to sit beside. Strength squares your Ascendant from Leo, two fixed signs, and fire and earth only work together once they've been properly introduced, so the card brings something your first impression doesn't naturally have. That something is visible heat. People get the calm, and a little later they get the confidence under it.

The instinct of a Taurus Ascendant is to hold back and let people come to you, which works, slowly. With Strength here you can afford to show more of yourself early, and you'll probably find the steadiness people already trust starting to read as quiet authority, the sort that makes a room settle when you sit down. The square is the catch. Fixed on fixed can look immovable, and if someone pushes you in a first meeting you may dig in and go blank-faced, which strangers read as cold or stubborn when you're really just uncomfortable.

It shows at a new job, where people work you out over weeks. It shows in meeting a partner's family, in haggling over a price, in any conversation where you'd normally say very little and let your manner do the work. It helps on a date with someone nervous, who'll feel safe with you fast. Let your face show what you think a beat sooner than you normally would.
rising.reversed:
Strength reversed can make a Taurus Ascendant look like a closed door. You're polite and calm and strangers get nothing back, so they decide you're either stubborn or not interested. Sometimes the Venus side overcorrects and you go very agreeable instead, nodding along to avoid friction until nobody can tell what you actually think. Either way the square between card and sign locks up, and your warmth stays indoors.

New workplaces bring it out most, especially where you're being sized up. You'll see it when someone challenges you in public and you go still and heavy and don't say a word. In the body it's the planted feet and the held breath. With new people it can take months for them to find out you're funny. Next time you meet someone, ask them one real question and let them see you react to the answer, a laugh, a frown, whatever's true.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns are proud of being quick. Mutable air, ruled by Mercury, you pick things up fast, talk to anyone, and have a clever way out of most rooms, and a good deal of who you are is built on that. Strength is fire, and fire and air feed each other. The card sits two signs from Gemini, a sextile, which gives you an easy opening. It still has to be used. Nothing about a sextile happens on its own.

What Strength asks of a Gemini Sun is a slower kind of courage. Yours is verbal. You can argue either side, charm your way past an awkward moment, change the subject so smoothly nobody notices. The card's courage is saying the one thing you mean and staying with it, without the joke at the end and without the second sentence that softens the first. The Lovers is Gemini's own card, and it's about choosing. Strength is about standing by the choice once it's made. You'll feel that as a kind of exposure, speaking plainly with no exit, and people tend to trust a Gemini who can do it a great deal.

At work it looks like the meeting where you'd usually hedge and could just say what you think. With a friend it's the time you were hurt and made a joke of it. With a brother or sister it may be an old conversation that keeps going round and round. Pick one thing you actually believe and say it in a single plain sentence, to someone who might disagree.
sun.reversed:
The reversed card leaves a Gemini Sun talking its way round everything. You've got an answer for every question and a reason for every change of plan, and underneath the cleverness there's nerves about being pinned to one position. Fire and air wind each other up, so the energy is high and scattered, lots of starts, lots of chat, very little that lands.

At work it's the pitch you've given so often you've stopped believing it, or the commitment you slid out of with a good excuse. In friendships it's being liked by many people and known by very few. A friend might say they never know where they stand with you, and you'll have a funny answer ready. Sleep goes thin and the mind races at two in the morning. When you catch yourself explaining, stop halfway, say what you actually want, and leave it there.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon can describe a feeling beautifully while it's still happening. You talk, you text, you look it up, you turn it into a story for a friend, and once it's got words on it you usually feel better. Mercury rules Gemini, so feelings go through your mind very fast, sometimes faster than you've actually felt them. Strength sits in easy sextile to your Moon, and fire gives air something to burn, so the card warms you without much resistance.

What it warms is the body, which a Gemini Moon tends to leave out of things. The card's kind of steadiness has no words in it. It belongs to someone who can sit beside something frightening and keep breathing. For you that means letting a feeling sit in your chest or your stomach for a while before you explain it to anyone, and it may feel odd, even a bit pointless, because you're used to fixing things with language. The trouble is that words can keep a feeling going round. You explain it well, you explain it again, and it's still there, because it was never really a thinking problem.

It shows at night, when one small worry turns into ten because your mind won't stop drafting. It shows with friends, when you make a joke of the thing that hurt. With a partner it can show as talking about the relationship at length and never saying the one simple thing. When you're upset, tell one person in a sentence or two, and then let them make you a cup of tea without adding anything.
moon.reversed:
With Strength reversed, a Gemini Moon talks a feeling to pieces and never quite has it. The analysis goes round, you look at the thing from six angles, and each new angle makes you more anxious. Fire and air feed each other too well here, the mind gets hot and fast and won't cool, and the restlessness can feel like energy when it's mostly fear.

It shows in sleep that won't come, a jumpy stomach, a phone that's always in your hand. With the people close to you, it can look like cleverness used to keep them at arm's length, and a friend may notice you're funnier than usual and much further away. Put the phone in another room for an evening, lie on the floor for ten minutes, and notice what you feel before you think anything about it.

rising.upright:
Quick is the word people tend to use about Gemini rising. Mercury rules your chart, and you come across as curious, funny, easy to talk to, and a little hard to hold, as if you might be across the room in a minute. Strength adds weight. Leo is fire, your Ascendant is air, and a sextile joins them, so things catch fast when you walk in, and the card gives people a sense that there's someone steady behind the quickness.

That's worth more than it sounds. Gemini rising gets underestimated a lot, because lightness looks like a lack of depth to anyone who hasn't known you long. With this card the charm and the substance arrive together. You might find yourself talking less and holding people's eye more, and it'll probably feel strange, because your instinct is to keep things moving and fill the gaps. The sextile only gives you the opening. You still have to go through it, which here means letting a first conversation slow down enough for someone to actually meet you.

It helps in interviews, where your answers can be clever or grounded and this card favours grounded. It helps on dates and in new friendships, where people remember how you made them feel long after they've forgotten your best line. With a new manager, being the calm one goes a long way. In the next first conversation you have, let one silence happen and don't rush to fill it.
rising.reversed:
Turned over, Strength can make Gemini rising come across as all patter. You talk fast to fill the space, deflect anything real with a joke, and the people you meet leave entertained and unsure whether they met you. Or nerves show through the charm and you over-explain, three reasons where one would do, which makes you look less sure than you are.

It shows at networking evenings and parties where you perform and go home tired. It shows in interviews where every answer is clever and none of them sounds quite like you. On a date it can come across as keeping the other person at a distance with wit, which they'll feel even if they laugh. When you're getting to know someone, ask one question and listen to the whole answer before you say anything back.

sun.upright:
A Cancer Sun knows itself through the people it looks after. Cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, your pride is in holding things together, the family, the friendship group, the team at work, usually from somewhere slightly out of sight. Strength belongs to the sign next door. Leo follows Cancer round the zodiac, and neighbouring signs have little in common, which means each has what the other is missing. Fire and water don't mix easily either. Put them together and you get steam, and it's worth saying where the steam is.

It's in being seen. Leo's strength is out in front, warm and obvious. Cancer's is protective and mostly happens behind the scenes, the phone call nobody knows you made, the dinner you quietly cooked for someone who was struggling. The Chariot is Cancer's own card, and its driver wears armour and holds his animals with no visible reins. Strength has no armour at all. That's the stretch for you, letting people see you being strong without putting the shell up first. The Cancer Suns I've known often find this harder than any amount of caring, because being visible feels a lot like being exposed.

At home it shows as being the one everyone leans on and nobody thinks to check on. At work it's the emotional labour that never appears on a performance review. With a parent, it might be a conversation where you're the grown-up in the room. Take credit for one thing you did for someone, out loud, in front of other people, and don't make a joke of it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, Strength can turn a Cancer Sun's care into a quiet kind of martyrdom. You're doing everything for everyone and keeping a private list of it, and the hurt builds because nobody's noticed. Or you pull right back into the shell and go moody, and the people around you are left guessing what they did. Fire and water hiss against each other, the confidence that should come up gets swamped by feeling, and you end up smaller than you are.

At home you mention how much you do, in a tone everyone recognises. At work you're overlooked and say nothing, then stew about it on the drive home. The body often carries it in the stomach. Ask for one specific thing from someone close to you, plainly, before the resentment has a chance to build, and let them do it their way.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon at home, feeling everything at full strength, remembering everything, needing a safe place to put it all. Strength is the card of Leo, the next sign along, a neighbour that shares almost nothing with you. That can be useful. Fire and water are opposites in this scheme, so there's steam where they touch, and what Leo has in plenty is the thing a Cancer Moon usually runs short of, which is the nerve to stay put when you're hurt.

Your instinct under pressure is to withdraw. Someone says something careless and you go quiet and back into the shell, and you might stay there for days while part of you waits to see if they notice. The card asks you to feel all of it and stay in the room anyway, which for a Cancer Moon is a genuinely brave thing to do. There's pride mixed into this too, and you'll recognise it. Cancer's hurt feelings and Leo's hurt pride are close cousins, and sometimes the withdrawal is as much about dignity as about pain.

This shows most at home, in the evening when a small comment lands wrong. It shows with your mother or whoever raised you, where old hurts get touched very easily. It shows in your stomach and your sleep. When someone hurts you, tell them the same day, while you're still a bit upset and in your own words, and then stay in the room while they answer.
moon.reversed:
When Strength reverses on a Cancer Moon, the water puts the fire out. You retreat so far into yourself that nothing gets in, and old hurts come back up, the thing someone said at a family dinner years ago, replayed in the car on the way home. A mood can run the whole household for days. The other version is clinging, needing reassurance that you're loved and feeling each small absence like a door shutting.

It comes out at home and around food, the fridge at night, the doona in the afternoon. It comes out with family, where you can go cold on someone and not say why. Toughening up has never worked on a Cancer Moon and it won't start working now. Look after yourself first, in the plainest way, a bath, a proper meal, a call to the one friend who gets it, and look at the hurt once you're warm.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes into a room sideways. You check who's there and whether it's safe, and strangers read you as kind, a bit shy, hard to get to know quickly. The Moon rules your chart, so your face shows the weather more than you'd like. Strength on your mask comes from the sign next door, Leo, which shares almost nothing with Cancer, and fire and water pull against each other, so expect some awkwardness in the fit.

What the card asks is that you come in facing forward. Cancer rising protects itself first, reading the room before offering anything, and people without the patience to wait sometimes decide you're cool or distant. Strength offers the confidence to show your warmth before you've checked everyone out, and there's some steam in that, because it feels exposed. You'll probably notice your instinct to hang back, and then notice that people respond well when you don't. Leo is generous by nature, and some of that generosity rubs off on how you arrive.

It shows in a new job, where the first week decides a lot. It shows at parties where you know one person, and on dates, where you'd usually ask all the questions and give very little away. With a partner's family it can help a great deal. Next time you're somewhere new, introduce yourself before anyone has the chance to introduce you.
rising.reversed:
Strength reversed on Cancer rising puts the shell up hard. You hang back so long the chance passes, and people read you as moody or distant when you're only nervous. Or the protectiveness points outward and you meet strangers already braced, taking small things as slights. The fire that could have warmed your manner gets doused, and you come across colder than you are.

At a new job there's the colleague who decides you're unfriendly before you've found your feet. At parties there's the evening spent in the kitchen with the one person you know. It can sit in the stomach and shoulders as a tense, guarded feeling that doesn't let go until you're home. At the next party or first day, offer something small about yourself early, where you grew up, what you did on the weekend, and let people respond to it.

sun.upright:
The Sun rules Leo, and Strength is Leo's own card, so a Leo Sun drawing it is about as close as the deck gets to a mirror. That's lovely, and it's also a lot of fire in one place. Same element, same sign, so the card turns up everything already in you, the generosity and courage and warmth, and alongside them the pride and the wish to be seen doing it.

Look at the picture for a second. She's alone with the lion. There's no crowd and nobody clapping. For a Leo Sun that's the interesting bit, because you're strong and you know it, and part of the pleasure has always been being seen. The card has no quarrel with that. It's pointing at the strength you'd still have in an empty room. I've seen a lot of Leo Suns get to their forties and realise the people who love them most were never all that impressed by the big moments. What they valued was the steadiness. Leo is fixed fire, the kind that keeps burning long after the flare, and this card is asking you to trust that side of yourself.

At work it shows when someone else takes credit for something you did and you have to decide whether to make a thing of it. With children, or anyone younger who looks up to you, it's the patience you show on an ordinary evening. In creative work it's finishing something that won't get much attention. Ask someone you trust what they actually value in you, and listen to the answer without correcting it.
sun.reversed:
With Strength reversed, a Leo Sun's pride bruises easily and shows it. A small slight becomes a wound, you push harder just so people can see you pushing, and the gentle strength turns into a performance of strength, loud and tiring for everyone including you. It can go the other way as well. The confidence thins out, you need a steady supply of praise to feel alright, and when it doesn't come you sulk or overwork.

At work it's needing to be the one who's right in the meeting. At home it can look like generosity with a hook in it, the favour that has to be thanked for properly. You may notice you're exhausted under the brightness. Put one piece of work out with someone else's name first, or with no name at all, and pay attention to how that feels.

moon.upright:
Pride and hurt sit very close together in a Leo Moon. You're warm and loyal and big-hearted with the people you love, and a Moon in the Sun's own sign wants to be looked at kindly. Being taken for granted stings more than you'll usually admit. Strength drawn for your tides is Leo's card meeting Leo in the feeling part of you, fire on fire, so everything runs warm, and when it's off, it runs dramatic.

What this card brings is a warmth you can give yourself. A Leo Moon usually looks outward for reassurance, a partner's attention, a friend remembering the thing that matters to you, a bit of praise after you've made an effort. There's nothing wrong with wanting that. The card is pointing out that you can also be quietly proud of yourself without anyone confirming it. Because it's your own element this won't feel like a lesson so much as a relief. You'll notice the need for applause easing a little, and you'll probably be nicer to the people around you as a result.

It shows with a partner when their attention drifts for a week and you have to decide whether to sulk. It shows around birthdays and anniversaries, the ones you care about more than you let on. It shows at work when your effort goes unmentioned. Next time you're waiting to be told you did well, write down what you did, and read it back to yourself before you go looking for anyone else's opinion.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon's need for warmth goes bottomless when this card is reversed. No amount of attention quite fills it, every small oversight lands as proof you don't matter, and sulking becomes a way of making people pay for not guessing. Sometimes it flips into proud silence, and you'd sooner suffer where everyone can see than say you needed something.

The people closest to you cop the moods. It can show as spending or eating to cheer yourself up, which works for about an hour. A friend might tell you you've seemed flat lately and you'll say you're fine. Pick the person whose attention you've been waiting for and do something warm for them first, without explaining why, and see how the sulk feels after that.

rising.upright:
Leo rising gets noticed in the doorway. The Sun rules your chart, and strangers usually clock presence first, the laugh, the hair, the way you take up space without apologising for it. Strength is your own sign's card, fire on fire, so drawing it for your mask turns that presence up. People meet warmth and confidence, and they meet it fast.

The card's gift here is that the warmth reads as real. Leo rising can shade into performance, especially when you're nervous, and people pick up the effort even when they couldn't name it. There's none of that in the picture. She isn't performing at all, she's just calm, and if anyone looks impressed it's the lion. When this card is working for you, strangers come away feeling steadier for having met you, and they'd follow you somewhere without quite knowing why. The risk with so much fire is the flip side, being too much for a quiet room. You'll know it's happening because you'll feel yourself switching it on.

It helps in interviews, where you're likely to come across as a natural leader. On first dates the temptation is to dazzle, and the card suggests warmth instead. At family events and weddings you tend to end up the centre of things whether you mean to or not. Walk into the next room you want to impress with the volume turned down, and let people come to you.
rising.reversed:
Strength upside down can make a Leo Ascendant look as though it's trying too hard. The warmth becomes a show you can't turn off, and strangers sense the effort under the charm. Or the front wobbles and you walk out of a room replaying whether they liked you, which is nothing like how anyone saw you and exactly how it feels.

You'll see it at parties where you're the life of the evening and go home hollow. It shows in interviews where you oversell, and on dates where you perform the whole night and never quite meet the person. The body gets tired from being on, and a quiet weekend afterwards can feel oddly flat. Go to one thing where nobody knows you, stay quiet for the first half hour, and see who comes over to talk.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns build themselves out of being good at things. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you're the one who spots the mistake nobody else saw, and you're proud of your work in a way that's almost always tangled up with criticising it. Strength belongs to Leo, the sign just before yours. Neighbouring signs have little in common, and each tends to have what the other lacks. Fire and earth aren't friends or enemies, so the card and your Sun have to be introduced.

What Leo has, and Virgo very often doesn't, is the confidence to think something's good and say so. You can do beautiful work and hand it in with a list of what's wrong with it. The card doesn't want you to lower your standards. It wants some warmth aimed back at the person doing the work, because usually it all flows the other way. The Hermit is Virgo's own card, and he works alone, out of sight, which suits a lot of Virgo Suns better than they'd say. Strength is out in the open with something wild and she doesn't apologise for being good at it.

At work it shows as redoing a thing that was already fine. With health it's scanning the body for what might be wrong. With the people you help, it can show as quietly judging them for needing it, which you'd hate anyone to notice. Tell one person about something you did well, and leave off the part where you explain what could have been better.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun with the card reversed turns the critical eye on itself and can't find the off switch. Nothing clears the bar. You redo, you check, you apologise for work that was good, and you call the tiredness diligence. With fire and earth failing to warm each other, the confidence never turns up and all that's left is the correcting.

At work it's perfectionism that stalls the project and makes every deadline harder than it needs to be. In the body it's a nervous gut and sleep broken up by lists, and food tracked to the point of worry. It spills onto other people too, a sharp note in your voice when a colleague's work isn't quite right. Send one thing out that's good enough, and don't open it again once it's gone.

moon.upright:
When a Virgo Moon is upset, the kitchen usually gets cleaned. Feelings come out as tasks for you, the drawer sorted, the list rewritten, a problem worked out on someone else's behalf, and it genuinely helps. Mercury rules Virgo, so your feelings go through the mind on their way, analysed for what went wrong and what you should have done. Strength sits in the sign before yours, a neighbour with little in common, and the fire and earth between them need a proper introduction before they'll help each other.

The card asks for something Virgo Moons find hard, which is holding a feeling without fixing it. Your reflex with a bad feeling is to treat it like a fault and look for the cause. Sometimes there is one. Often there isn't, or there's one you can't change, and the fixing just keeps you busy while the feeling sits there untouched. Strength's way is warmer and slower. You let the thing be there, unsolved, the way you'd sit with an upset friend without handing them a plan.

Your gut, your shoulders and your sleep are usually the first to know. At home it can show as tidying that gets a bit frantic. With people you care for, it shows as kindness you hand out freely and very rarely aim at yourself. When something's bothering you, sit down for ten minutes with a cup of tea and do nothing useful at all.
moon.reversed:
Worry takes the wheel when Strength reverses on a Virgo Moon. Every feeling becomes a fault report, you go back over what you said and did looking for the mistake, and the tidying and list-making tip into something compulsive that makes the anxiety worse. No warmth reaches the worry, only more picking at it.

You'll feel it in a gut that knots and sleep chewed through by the next day's jobs. It shows as care for everyone except you, and sometimes as sharpness with a partner about how things ought to be done. Friends may notice you apologising for things that aren't your fault. A better system won't fix this. Put a hand on your stomach, breathe slowly for a minute, and say to yourself what you'd say to a friend who was this worried.

rising.upright:
Neat, observant and a little reserved is how Virgo rising usually comes across. Mercury rules your chart, and strangers notice the care first, the tidy clothes, the good questions, the sense you've already taken in everything in the room. Strength is the card of the sign right before Virgo, a neighbour that shares very little with you, and fire and earth only work together once someone's done the introductions. So the card brings something your first impression doesn't usually have, which is warmth that doesn't wait for permission.

Virgo rising tends to assess first and warm up later. Plenty of people never get to later, because they've already decided you're cool or hard to please. With Strength here the warmth can come through before the assessment is done, and you'll probably find people relaxing around you much faster than usual. The card also brings some of the confidence Virgo rising tends to hide. You're quick to point out what you haven't done yet. Strength would like people to see what you have.

It shows in job interviews, where you tend to undersell. It shows in new friendships that could go somewhere if you let people see you enjoying yourself. On a date it can be the difference between seeming careful and seeming interested. Next time you meet someone, find one thing you like about them early, and tell them.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising with the card reversed can make strangers feel checked over. Even if you never say what you noticed, they can tell you noticed it. The warmth stays behind the assessment, and you come across as prim or unimpressed when mostly you're nervous. Or you go the other way and undersell yourself so thoroughly that people believe you.

On a first day somewhere, your reserve gets read as disapproval, and the same happens in first meetings with a partner's friends. It can show as a tense, fault-finding restlessness that won't let an introduction just be nice. Underneath is usually your own fear of not being good enough, pointed outward. Walk into the next room looking for something to like about it, and mention that first.

sun.upright:
A Libra Sun builds itself in company. Cardinal air, ruled by Venus, you find yourself through other people, the fair arrangement, the good conversation, the room that's comfortable because you made it so. Strength sits two signs from Libra, a sextile, and fire and air feed each other, so this is an easy card for your Sun. Easy openings still have to be taken, though, and this one asks for something a Libra Sun doesn't often volunteer.

That something is a position. You see both sides of most things, often better than anyone, and you'll usually choose peace over being right. There's a bit of tarot history you might like here. In older decks Justice, Libra's own card, was number eight and Strength was eleven, and the Rider-Waite deck swapped them, so the two have always sat close. Justice weighs things. Strength has already decided and is getting on with it, calmly, with no need for anyone to agree. For a Libra Sun that can feel almost rude. It isn't, and it's often what lets people trust you with something difficult.

It shows in decisions you've put off to keep everyone comfortable, and in a relationship where you give more than you let on. At work it's the idea you haven't pushed because someone might disagree. With friends it can look like always being the one who adjusts. In the next meeting, say what you actually think, once and kindly, and leave it on the table.
sun.reversed:
When this card reverses, a Libra Sun can vanish into everyone else's preferences. The wish to be liked starts making the decisions, and you bend so far to keep things smooth that you lose track of what you wanted in the first place. Fire and air whip each other up, a lot of charming activity and very little firm ground, and every choice gets put off in case it upsets someone.

In relationships it's resentment under the niceness, a score you'd never admit to keeping. At work it's agreeing in the room and fuming in the car. The body holds it as a low tension that's never quite off duty. Say no to one thing you'd normally agree to, warmly and without a long explanation, and let the other person be a little put out.

moon.upright:
Conflict lands in a Libra Moon's body before anyone's raised their voice. You feel tension in a room like a change in temperature, and what settles you is harmony, pleasant company, the sense that everyone's alright with you. Venus rules Libra, so beauty and ease genuinely soothe you. Strength sits in sextile to your Moon, fire warming air, and it brings something this Moon is often short of, which is the nerve to let a bit of tension exist without rushing in to fix it.

Your reflex when someone's upset with you is to smooth it over fast. Apologise, agree, make it nice again, even when the nice version isn't the true one. The card's warmth steadies you enough to leave the discomfort alone for a while and check what you actually feel. The angle between the signs is friendly, so this doesn't take much of a wrench. What you get from it is a self that doesn't dissolve the moment someone frowns at you, and that tends to make you better company as well.

It shows in arguments you end early just to stop the bad feeling. It shows in friendships where you're always the go-between, and at family gatherings where you manage everyone's mood and go home wrung out. It can show in your sleep after an evening of being agreeable. When you notice yourself reaching to smooth something over, count to ten and say what you feel first.
moon.reversed:
A Libra Moon with Strength reversed keeps the peace by disappearing from it. You swallow your own feelings to avoid a cross word, so often you stop being sure what they are, and the harmony you're protecting goes hollow because you aren't really in it. Fire and air wind each other into a nervy over-accommodation, agreeing and soothing while the resentment pools underneath.

It shows with a partner, where you've gone along with things so long you've lost track of your own tastes. You could list everyone else's preferences to the letter and struggle to name yours. After a social evening there's a jittery tension that won't let you rest. When a small disagreement starts between other people, stay out of it and let it run, and see what happens when you aren't the one holding everything together.

rising.upright:
Libra rising is easy to like on sight. Venus rules your chart, and people meet someone gracious and well put together, tuned to the other person, very good at making a stranger feel interesting. Strength on your mask is a friendly sextile, fire feeding air, and it gives all that charm a centre, so people come away feeling steadied as well as welcomed.

A Libra Ascendant's risk is mirroring too well. You become whatever the other person seems to want, agreeable and pleasant and a bit hard to locate afterwards. Strength gives your manner a warmth that's clearly your own and doesn't shift with the company. It's a small difference and people feel it. They trust someone who has opinions and holds them kindly, and with this card you're likely to be exactly that person. The sextile makes it easy, as long as you let a real view show early.

It shows in negotiations, where you'd usually give ground to keep things nice. It shows in interviews for roles that need someone decisive. On first dates it's the difference between being charming and being known. Before your next meeting with someone new, decide one thing you think about the subject, and say it within the first five minutes.
rising.reversed:
Strength upside down on a Libra Ascendant can make the charm run on empty. You're pleasant to everyone and nobody's quite sure who you are. You shape yourself to the company, strangers like a version of you that isn't very real, and fire and air froth up into an agreeableness that's exhausting to keep going.

At work it's being popular and not taken seriously. In dating it's adjusting so much in the first few weeks that the other person falls for someone you're pretending to be. After social events there's a tiredness that's out of all proportion to what you did. Friends of friends may call you lovely and then admit they couldn't name a single thing you believe. Disagree with someone warmly in your next real conversation, about something small, and don't take it back.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns keep their strength where nobody can see it. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, you build yourself around depth and control, and there's pride in being the one who feels everything and shows almost nothing. Strength squares Scorpio from Leo, three signs apart and both fixed, so this is two strong wills meeting and neither is designed to give way. The elements are at odds as well, fire against water. Expect steam.

Your strength is held in reserve. The card's is out in the open, warm and unarmed, a woman with her bare hands on a lion and no weapon anywhere in sight. That's a real challenge for a Scorpio Sun, because being visible feels like being exposed, and being exposed feels like danger. The square asks a pointed question, which is whether all that control is strength or armour you've got used to wearing. Mars is Scorpio's traditional ruler and it's always ready to defend. Strength's defence is that she doesn't seem to need one. Put a little of her ease into your intensity and you lose none of the power, and a lot more people can come close.

At work it shows where you're holding knowledge or influence tightly because that feels safer. In an intimate relationship it's the part of you your partner still hasn't seen after years. With an old grudge, it's the question of whether it's protecting you or just taking up room. Tell one person something you'd normally keep to yourself, and don't watch their face for a reaction.
sun.reversed:
For a Scorpio Sun, the reversed card turns strength into grip. You control what you can, withhold what you can, and fight a slow, quiet war with whoever's nearest, through silence, through information, through the look that says you've noticed. Mars rules Scorpio and it doesn't forget a slight. Fire and water hiss against each other, and the warmth that could soften you boils off before it arrives.

You'll recognise it in a grudge you tend like a pet, and in intimacy withheld to keep the upper hand. At work it's knowledge held back that would help other people do their jobs. The body carries it as held breath and a clenched jaw. Say one vulnerable thing to one safe person, and let them take it however they take it, without managing their response.

moon.upright:
Her hands are right at the lion's mouth. For a Scorpio Moon that's the part of the picture that matters, because it's a picture of trust, and trust is the hardest thing you do. You feel in extremes and show very little, and loyalty matters to you more than almost anything, so a betrayal, real or suspected, can turn you to stone for years. Mars rules Scorpio, which keeps this Moon half ready for a fight. Strength squares your Moon, both fixed signs, and water and fire are natural opponents, so the card presses right on the place you guard hardest.

What it presses on is the clamp. Your instinct with a strong feeling is to hold it down and let nobody see, and you're very good at it. The card asks whether you could hold the feeling gently instead, let it move a little, even let someone near it. That's a big ask, because letting a feeling move can feel like losing control of it. What tends to happen, though, is that the feelings you don't clamp down on pass through, and the ones you do clamp down on stay and go sour.

It shows around trust, the friend who's been on probation for two years, the partner you keep quietly testing. It shows in sleep, when the jaw is tight and the mind replays a conversation. With family it can show as an old wound nobody's allowed to mention. Let one person who's earned it see something you'd usually keep sealed, and don't take it back the next day.
moon.reversed:
With Strength reversed on a Scorpio Moon, a hurt goes underground and stays there. It hardens into a grudge, trust snaps shut, and you watch people for signs they're about to let you down, which they sometimes then do, because being watched is hard to live with. The water smothers the fire, and the warmth that might have reached you never gets through.

It shows as suspicion of people who've done nothing wrong, and as closeness given and then taken back. It shows in the jaw, the gut and the shoulders. A partner may feel they're permanently on trial. Tell the person you've been watching what you've been afraid of, in a quiet moment, without accusing them of anything, and let them answer.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising doesn't give much away in a first meeting. You watch, you listen, and strangers often feel they've been read before they've said anything. Mars rules your chart, and Pluto does too in the modern scheme, and there's force held back behind the calm. Strength squares your Ascendant, fixed against fixed, and it brings fire to a water sign, so there's friction here, and it's worth working with.

What the card adds is heat to go with the depth. A Scorpio entrance can come across as intense and a bit cold, powerful and hard to approach, and Strength warms it enough that people feel drawn in where they'd usually be kept at a distance. You lose none of the intensity. It just stops making people work so hard to reach you. For a sign that treats openness as a risk, the stretch is letting some warmth show before you've decided whether someone's safe. The square means it won't feel natural. It may feel a bit like leaving a door unlocked.

It shows at a new job, where people decide early whether you're an ally or a threat. It shows in negotiations, where people give more ground to someone they like. On a first date it can make you seem safe as well as interesting, which is a rare mix. Smile at someone in the first minute of your next meeting, before you've worked them out.
rising.reversed:
Strength upside down on Scorpio rising makes the guard very visible. You come into a room already checking it, and people pick up on the watching before they notice anything else about you. A few find it intriguing. More find it a bit frightening and keep their distance, and you read their distance as proof you were right to be careful.

A new team may go quiet when you walk in. A first date can feel like a test the other person didn't know they'd signed up for. With neighbours or new in-laws, a coolness settles that nobody meant. Your chart ruler is Mars, which reacts fast to threat, even threat that isn't there. At the next gathering, sit with your back to the room for once, and ask someone about something they love.

sun.upright:
There's a restlessness in a Sagittarius Sun that you'd probably call freedom, and most of the time you'd be right. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you build yourself by going further, the next idea, the next country, the truth said out loud even when the room didn't want it. Strength is fire too. Leo and Sagittarius sit four signs apart, a trine, and a same-element pairing like this flows easily and amplifies what's there, the optimism and the generosity and the habit of overdoing things.

What Leo's fire has that yours often doesn't is staying power. Leo is fixed. It burns in one place for a long time, where Sagittarius tends to set a whole hillside going and move on. The card's courage is the kind that stays in the room when things get dull or difficult, and it's a kind of bravery a Sagittarius Sun doesn't always rate, because from outside it doesn't look like much. Temperance is your sign's own card, and it's about mixing things in the right amounts. Strength asks you to mix some staying into all the going. Most Sagittarians I've read for find that the life they're proudest of by fifty had a few long commitments in it.

At work it shows in the project you've half left for something shinier. In love it's the relationship where you keep an exit open without quite admitting it. In arguments your honesty can land harder than you meant. Pick the thing you're most tempted to walk away from and give it three more months of real effort before you decide.
sun.reversed:
The fire scatters when this card reverses for a Sagittarius Sun. Every time something gets hard or boring you're already somewhere else, and it looks like freedom from outside and feels a bit like running from inside. Fire on fire runs away with itself, lots of momentum and nothing to hold it, promises made in a great mood and dropped when the mood changes.

It leaves a trail of half-finished plans and people waiting for a call back. It shows in blunt remarks you'd call honesty and other people feel as carelessness. Money can go the same way, spent on the next big thing before the last one's paid off. Choose one promise you've made and haven't kept, go back to it, and do it properly, however small it is.

moon.upright:
Heavy feelings make a Sagittarius Moon itch. You steady yourself with movement and humour and a bigger picture, and when something painful arrives your instinct is to reframe it, find the lesson, book a trip, anything that keeps things moving. Jupiter rules Sagittarius, and Jupiter's comfort is always a bit larger than life. Strength sits in easy trine to your Moon, fire meeting fire, so the card works with your warmth and doesn't fight it.

What it gives you is a way to stay with a feeling without feeling trapped. That distinction matters to a Sagittarius Moon, because you've probably always assumed that sitting with something heavy means getting stuck in it. Strength's fire is steady and it doesn't go anywhere, and it's still fire. You can stay put for an evening with grief or disappointment and it won't put you out. Because the elements agree, this may come more easily than you'd expect. The hard part is resisting the urge to leave the feeling halfway through.

It shows when something disappointing happens and you're making jokes about it within the hour. It shows in relationships you keep light because light is easier. It shows in a body that gets restless when it's asked to rest, legs jiggling, phone out. When you want to bolt from a feeling, stay with it one more hour before you do anything, and see what's left.
moon.reversed:
A Sagittarius Moon under the reversed card runs from every hard feeling it has. Grief gets outrun with plans, disappointment with jokes, a bad week with a big night out, and the buoyancy that usually saves you becomes a way of never landing. There's a brightness to it that people close to you might find a little manic.

Relationships get kept deliberately loose so they can't ask much of you. The body treats stillness like a threat, late nights, too much of whatever's on offer, and sleep tends to suffer first. A friend might say you seem great, and you might almost believe it. Spend one evening at home with no plans and no screen, and let whatever you've been outrunning catch up with you somewhere comfortable.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open and friendly and probably mid-story. With Jupiter ruling your chart, strangers get warmth, enthusiasm, a laugh, maybe an opinion they didn't ask for, and they tend to like you on the spot. Strength on your mask is a trine, fire on fire, so it slides into all that easily and adds something steady underneath.

What a Sagittarius Ascendant can lack in a first meeting is weight. You're friendly with everyone and can seem attached to no one, and people sometimes wonder whether you'll remember them tomorrow. The card's fixed warmth helps with that. People come away charmed and also feeling you meant it, that you'd actually turn up if they rang. When it works, you're still the expansive, generous one in the room, with a reliability that makes people want to trust you with something. The risk with doubled fire is being a bit much, too loud for a small room or too blunt with someone sensitive.

At a new job people will like you fast and then wait to see if you follow through. On first dates, and in groups where you're the one everyone warms to, it gives the warmth somewhere to settle. It can help in teaching or speaking to a crowd. At the next gathering, stay half an hour longer than you planned and spend it talking to one person.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on a Sagittarius Ascendant, the friendliness blows straight through. You're warm with everyone and there with nobody, promising to catch up and meaning it at the time, and then gone. Or the bluntness sharpens, and something you say as a joke lands as an insult, and you don't notice because you've already moved on to the next person.

People warm to you quickly and then can't quite hold you. A new friend may start treating your invitations like the weather, nice when they happen and not something to plan around. At work your enthusiasm gets noticed, and so does the follow-through that didn't happen. Follow up on one thing you promised someone new, however small, before the end of the week.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns build themselves the long way. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you want to make something that lasts and be respected for it, and you're proud of carrying what other people would put down. Strength sits five signs from Capricorn, a quincunx, which means the two have almost nothing in common and need constant small adjustments to get along. Fire and earth don't naturally help or hurt each other. They have to be introduced.

The awkwardness is about effort. For a Capricorn Sun, strength usually means endurance, grinding through, doing the hard thing without complaining. The card's strength doesn't look like effort at all. The Devil is Capricorn's own card, and in it two people stand in chains. In Strength the only thing tying the woman to the lion is a chain of flowers. That's quite a difference in how power works, and you'll probably feel it. Part of you trusts only what's been paid for in sweat, and the card is asking whether you could let something be easy and still count it. That's hard for Saturn people, and worth the adjustment.

At work you may be the last to leave and a little suspicious of anyone who isn't. In the body it's the shoulders, knees and back carrying more than they need to. With a parent it can be needing approval for work they'll never fully understand. Take one afternoon off in the middle of the week, tell nobody why, and don't make the hours up later.
sun.reversed:
Discipline turns into a sentence you're serving when a Capricorn Sun draws this card reversed. You drive yourself without let-up, measure your worth by what you produce, and treat any softness toward yourself as weakness. The quincunx grinds, fire and earth never quite meeting, and the warmth that could ease things stays out of reach.

It shows in overwork that hollows you out and gets called commitment. It shows in a coldness toward yourself you'd be ashamed to aim at a colleague. The body gets pushed past what's sensible, a stiff neck, poor sleep, a cold you won't take time off for. Ask someone to help with something you could easily do yourself, and let them do it without checking their work.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon copes. That's mostly what you do with feelings, you get on top of them, handle it, make sure nobody has to worry about you. Saturn rules Capricorn, and a Saturn Moon often learned young that relying on people was risky. Strength sits at a quincunx to your Moon, an awkward angle between two signs with little in common, and fire and earth have no natural bond, so the card keeps nudging you toward something that doesn't come naturally.

That something is tenderness toward yourself. Your instinct with a hard feeling is to manage it, be stoic, deal with it alone so nobody sees you wobble. The card suggests being gentle with the feeling as well as controlling it, and you may find that faintly embarrassing. It isn't weakness. The woman in the picture is completely in charge and there's nothing hard about her, and that combination is on offer to you too. The quincunx means it takes practice, a small adjustment over and over, until being kind to yourself stops feeling like letting yourself off.

It shows in the help you won't ask for, even from someone who'd be glad to give it. It shows in grief handled by working longer hours. In the body it's a kind of armour across the shoulders, and sleep that stays light because part of you is still on duty. Next time someone offers to help, say yes before you've had time to work out why you don't need it.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Capricorn Moon seals itself off. Feeling gets filed under inefficiency and need under failure, and you handle everything alone until the loneliness becomes its own low ache. The quincunx pulls hard, and the warmth always arrives at the wrong angle to reach you. Some Capricorn Moons have been like this since primary school.

It shows in help you'd refuse even while you're struggling to stay afloat, and in grief buried under the next job. It shows in a set jaw and shoulders that won't come down, and in a partner or friend who's stopped offering because you always say you're fine. Tell one safe person you're finding something hard, in those words, and don't follow it straight away with how you're handling it.

rising.upright:
There's a formality to Capricorn rising that strangers pick up straight away. Saturn rules your chart, and people see someone capable, contained and a little reserved, not giving much away until you've decided they're worth it. Strength on your mask sits at a quincunx, five signs from Capricorn, an awkward fit, and fire and earth need introducing before they'll work together. So the card's warmth doesn't slide in easily. It has to be adjusted to.

The benefit is real, though. A Capricorn Ascendant tends to be respected and kept at a slight distance, and plenty of people would like to know you better and don't quite dare. Strength offers a way to be taken seriously and be warm at the same time, which you may have assumed was a trade. When it's working, people meet someone solid who is also clearly glad to see them, and they remember that. You'll feel the awkwardness of the angle the moment you let your face relax in a meeting, as if you've dropped something, and it gets easier each time.

It shows in interviews, where your competence is obvious and your warmth usually isn't. It shows with a new team, who'll respect you anyway and might like you too if you let them. On dates, it can turn seeming serious into seeming safe. Let someone see you laugh in the first five minutes of your next meeting, at something that's actually funny.
rising.reversed:
Strength reversed on a Capricorn Ascendant can freeze the first impression. The reserve hardens into something austere, and strangers read you as cold or unimpressed or quietly judging them. The warmth stays locked behind duty and status, so you come across like a closed office, correct and not very welcoming. Sometimes status does the talking for you, the title dropped early, the name of the firm.

People keep things formal with you and go elsewhere for friendliness, and some of them would have liked you a great deal. Staff junior to you may not realise you're approachable. With a partner's friends you're polite and forgettable. It sits in the body as posture that's a bit too upright. Ask someone new for their advice about something small, and take it.

sun.upright:
An Aquarius Sun stands a little apart, usually on purpose. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn in the old scheme and Uranus in the modern one, you build yourself around principles and ideas and the groups you believe in, and there's pride in seeing the pattern while everyone else is caught up in how they feel. Strength is the card of Leo, your opposite sign, the other end of the same axis. Fire and air are friendly elements, so this is a pull toward balance, and it won't feel like a fight.

Aquarius cares about people in general. Leo cares about the person in front of it, warmly and specifically and without much interest in the principle. The card asks you to bring your big, fair-minded care down to one human being at a time, and you may find that harder than caring about a whole cause. Both signs are fixed, so both are stubborn, and there's pride at each end of the axis. Leo's is in being loved. Yours is in being right, or at least in being free. The Star is your own card, hopeful and generous in a broad, open-sky way, and Strength is close-up and personal.

It shows where you're brilliant about humanity and a little cool with the actual people nearby. It shows in a partner who sometimes feels they come second to your friends or your causes. At work it can look like being fair to everyone and close to no one. Do something warm and specific for one person, something that would only make sense for them.
sun.reversed:
Detachment can harden into a cool superiority when an Aquarius Sun draws Strength reversed. You retreat into principle and the bigger picture exactly when something personal needs you, and the independence that looks admirable from outside is sometimes just a way of not having to feel. Fire and air whip each other up into a clever, chilly certainty.

Relationships get kept at arm's length by argument. Contrarianism creeps in, disagreeing partly to stay separate. There's a body you forget you have, because so much of you lives in your head. A friend in a bad patch might get a long, thoughtful message from you and never get a visit. Saturn is your traditional ruler, and Saturn knows people need steady, ordinary care as well as good ideas. Ring someone you've been meaning to call, and ask how they actually are.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs air around its feelings. You deal with emotion by stepping back and understanding it, and you can be oddly calm in a crisis because you've already risen above it and started working out what to do. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, this Moon likes independence and gets twitchy when closeness comes with conditions. Strength is Leo's card, and Leo sits directly opposite, the same axis from the other end. Fire and air get on well, so the card doesn't fight your Moon. It fills in the half you tend to leave out.

That half is warmth, close up and personal. Your reflex with a feeling is to observe it, and that keeps you steady, and it also keeps you a little absent from your own heart. Leo feels things from right in the middle of them, loudly, with no distance at all. The card asks you to come down into a feeling now and then, including the messy, needy, tender ones, and that may feel unnervingly close. It's also where most of the warmth you're missing tends to be.

It shows when someone needs you emotionally and you go cool and sensible. It shows in friendships where you're everyone's calm friend and nobody's close one. It shows in how you cope with being ill or worn out, which is usually alone. When someone tells you how they feel, tell them how you feel back, before you offer any perspective.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, an Aquarius Moon vanishes into its head. Feelings get analysed so thoroughly you lose track of what they were, closeness starts to look like a trap, and you pull back from the people who most want to be near you. Fire and air spin up a bright, detached calm that's quite lonely underneath. Old hurts, especially from friendships, can sit for years unexamined, because examining them would mean feeling them.

Relationships get kept cool and deniable, and emotional distance gets called independence. The body barely registers, because you're so busy thinking. A partner may say they can't reach you. Let one person be properly close for an evening, phones off, no debate, and when the urge to leave comes, notice it and stay.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as its own thing. Friendly, a bit detached, hard to put in a category, warm to everyone and close to nobody in particular. Saturn and Uranus sit behind your chart, and there's a cool independence in how you meet people that some find refreshing and some find hard to read. Strength on your mask comes from the opposite sign, Leo facing Aquarius, and fire and air get on, so this adds something easily.

What it adds is warmth aimed at one person. An Aquarius Ascendant treats everyone the same, which is fair, and can leave each person feeling like one of many. Leo's warmth is specific. It makes the person in front of you feel singled out. When the card is working, you're still the original, independent person people expect, and the stranger across from you feels properly noticed. Conversations go further than they usually do, and faster. Both signs are fixed, so you may resist this a little, because paying close attention to one person can feel like playing favourites.

It shows at parties where you move round the room and connect with no one. It shows on dates, where friendliness can read as lack of interest. It shows with a new team who can't tell whether you like them. In your next conversation with a stranger, remember one detail they tell you and ask about it before you leave.
rising.reversed:
Strength reversed on an Aquarius Ascendant makes the detachment go cold. You meet people from behind glass, friendly and obviously elsewhere, and the originality tips into being contrary for its own sake. Whatever warmth you have gets spread so thin that nobody feels it.

People find you interesting and unreachable. Colleagues respect your ideas and don't think to invite you to lunch. New friendships stay at the chatting stage for years. On dates there's a politeness that feels like a door held shut. At a party you'll talk to everyone for five minutes and leave without anyone's number. It can be lonely, and you may not admit that even to yourself. Pick one person you've met recently and follow up with them, one to one, about something they said.

sun.upright:
A Pisces Sun takes the shape of whatever room it's in. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you know yourself through compassion and imagination and a sense that the line between you and other people is thin. Strength sits five signs from Pisces, a quincunx, two signs with almost nothing in common, and fire and water have always been at odds, so there's steam here and some awkwardness. It's worth naming, because most of the reading lives there.

What the card brings is edges. Your strength is empathy, going soft, giving way to what's needed. The card's strength is warm and definite, someone who knows exactly where she ends and the lion begins. You'll feel the stretch, the part of you that merges meeting a card that says you're allowed to be a separate, solid person with wants of your own. The Moon is Pisces's own card, all shifting light and things half seen, which is a world you know well. Many Pisces Suns I've known assume that firmer edges would make them less kind. Usually it makes them kinder, because they stop running on empty.

It shows where you give until there's nothing left. It shows in a friendship or family role where you soak up other people's feelings as if they were yours. At work it shows as drifting when a decision is needed and hoping someone else will make it. Next time someone asks for your help, wait an hour before you answer, and use the hour to work out whether you actually want to.
sun.reversed:
The edges go completely when Strength reverses on a Pisces Sun. You merge with whoever you're with, take on feelings that aren't yours, give past empty and call it love, and the self that should hold steady washes away. The quincunx pulls awkwardly and the fire hisses out against the water, so the warmth that might steady you has nothing to hold on to.

You'll see it in relationships where you lose yourself, and in escapes into sleep or screens or a drink when real life gets sharp. The body feels foggy and drained. Friends and family may be leaning on you in ways that suit them and not you. Say one clear no to something you'd usually agree to, kindly, and hold it for a whole day.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon can walk into a room and feel what everyone in it is feeling before anyone's spoken. Your feelings have very few walls. You soak up the mood of a person, a household, a whole train carriage, and you're soothed by retreat, by music and water and sleep, by drifting somewhere softer. Jupiter rules Pisces, with Neptune as its modern ruler. Strength sits at a quincunx to your Moon, and fire meeting water makes steam, so the card pushes you toward something that doesn't come naturally.

It pushes toward a centre. Your reflex with a big feeling is to open to it completely and go wherever it takes you, and that's part of why you're so kind and so easily overwhelmed. Strength offers a warm, steady place inside you that can feel all of it and still stay standing, and still know which feelings are yours. For a Pisces Moon that's an unfamiliar idea, because losing yourself in feeling is so familiar it seems like who you are. It needn't be. The quincunx means the adjustment is small and constant, and it does get easier.

It shows when you've absorbed someone else's bad day and can't tell it from your own. It shows in the way you escape overwhelm, into sleep or a screen or a long bath. With a partner it shows as taking on their moods and losing track of yours. When the feelings flood in, put your feet flat on the floor and ask yourself whose feeling this is before you do anything else.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Pisces Moon can go under. You absorb everyone's emotions until you've no idea which are yours, you get swamped by moods you can't name, and you slip away into sleep or fantasy or anything softer than the flood. The water puts the fire out entirely, and the warm centre that could steady you never forms. Some Pisces Moons start avoiding people altogether under this card, because being around anyone is too loud.

It shows in relationships where your edges disappear, and in a leaky exhaustion from carrying feelings that were never yours. The body gets foggy and hard to come back into. Before you pick up anyone else's problem, write down three things you feel, just yours, and put the note somewhere you'll see it.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly and takes its colour from whoever's nearby. Strangers get gentleness, a dreamy, receptive quality, someone who seems to understand without being told, and with Jupiter and Neptune behind your chart there's something hard to pin down about you. Strength on your mask sits at a quincunx to your sign, an awkward fit, and fire and water pull in opposite directions, so the card's warmth arrives with some friction.

A Pisces Ascendant can mirror people so well that they never meet you. You become agreeable, vague, easy to be with and easy to walk over. Strength gives the softness a spine, a warmth that's clearly present and clearly somebody. When it lands, you keep your gentleness and gain a centre, and people feel your kindness and also feel there's a definite person offering it. The quincunx makes this feel like effort at first, and you may be surprised how well people take it when you have a view.

It shows in interviews, where you tend to fade into what they want. It shows in groups where you become whatever's needed, and on dates where you agree with everything and go home unsure what you like. With a new flatmate or colleague it sets the pattern early. Say where you'd like to sit, what you'd like to drink, which film you want to see, and don't add 'if that's alright'.
rising.reversed:
The doorway dissolves when Strength reverses on Pisces rising. You become whoever you're with so completely that strangers never actually meet you, and the softness tips into vagueness, a presence that slips through people's hands. The warmth that could make you real to them never quite takes shape, and steams off against all that water.

People find you gentle and impossible to locate. You may have no fixed opinion in company, and get walked over by people who can tell you won't object. At work it can mean being handed the jobs nobody else wants, because you won't say no. Some people take advantage of that without really meaning to, simply because you never push back. Keep one opinion that stays yours whoever you're with, and say it out loud at least once.

1.upright:
The first house is the body and the way you carry it, the face you walk in with, how you start things. It's an angular house, a corner of the chart, so whatever's drawn here shows. Its natural sign is Aries and its ruler is Mars, and Leo and Aries are four signs apart, a trine, both fire. So Strength doesn't have to work to belong here. It speaks the house's language, and it turns the volume up.

What changes is how you begin. Mars in the first house pushes through the door. Strength doesn't push. It has the confidence of someone who's already sure, and you'll probably notice people responding to a steadiness in you before you've done anything much. Things you'd normally have to fight for can open with less effort. Mercury has its joy in this house as well, so the way you speak as you arrive counts for more than usual. Doubled fire carries a risk, though. Confidence can tip into bravado, and the same energy that warms a room can overheat it.

In the body this is energy that lasts when it's looked after kindly, fitness built by turning up regularly with no punishment involved. In how you meet challenges, it's facing them without bracing for a fight. In how you look, it can show as standing up straighter without trying. When you start something new, lead with the calm and let the push wait.
1.reversed:
Reversed in the first house, strength wobbles right at the front door. The easy confidence tips into swagger, or it drains away and you hang back from things you could handle without much trouble.
