Fire on fire runs hot once the balance is gone. You either come in too strong, or the flame gutters and you doubt a strength that's plainly there.

Because the first house is so visible, other people see it. They see the bravado or the hesitation, and either one gets in the way of how you start things. In the body it can show as tension, or as a flat, worn-down tiredness that no amount of coffee touches. Stop performing and stop doubting, both at once, and start the next thing at an ordinary pace, with an ordinary amount of fuss.

2.upright:
Money you can actually count sits in the second house, along with the worth you feel in yourself, and the two are more tangled up than most people like to admit. It's succedent, a house for building up and holding on. Its natural sign is Taurus, ruled by Venus, and Leo squares Taurus with both signs fixed, which is friction that makes you do something. Fire and earth don't have a natural bond, so they need introducing, and around money that introduction can be a bit abrupt.

The tension is between security and self-respect. Taurus in the second house wants to feel safe through what it owns. Leo wants to feel good about who it is, and it's generous, sometimes to the point of flashiness. Strength here asks you to base your sense of worth on something steadier than the balance, so a thin stretch doesn't feel like a verdict on you and a good one doesn't go straight to your head. That's the square doing its work, two fixed signs grinding away until something better comes out of it.

With actual money this can look like spending and saving from a settled place, with less fear in it and less show. With pay, it can be the confidence to ask for what the work is worth, calmly and without apologising. With self-worth, it's knowing your value on a day when nothing's gone right. Before you buy something to cheer yourself up, wait a day and see whether you still want it.
2.reversed:
When the card reverses in the second house, worth wobbles and money gets anxious. Self-worth collapses into what you earn or own, a low balance feels like proof of something, and you either grip hard out of fear or spend to show you're doing fine. The square grinds, fire and earth failing to warm each other, and there's no settled confidence underneath the numbers.

It turns up as spending to feel better and saving out of dread, sometimes both in the same week. It turns up in undercharging, or in a pay conversation you keep putting off, and in comparing yourself to friends who earn more. Write down what you're good at, separately from what you're paid for it, and read the list before your next conversation about money.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house, the texts and emails and chats over the fence, along with learning, brothers and sisters, neighbours, and the short trips that fill an ordinary week. It's cadent, a house of learning and adjusting. Its natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury, and the Moon has its joy here, so there's feeling under the chatter. Leo is a sextile from Gemini, fire and air feeding each other, which makes this an easy placement. It's an opening, though, and you still have to use it.

What Strength gives your voice is warmth and weight. The third house on its own can be quick and clever and a bit scattered. With this card, what you say lands more steadily, and you'll probably find you can calm a tense exchange where you'd normally win it or dodge it. That's useful, because a lot of ordinary life happens in small exchanges, the neighbour who's cross about the bins, the sibling who knows how to wind you up, the colleague who emails in capitals. With the Moon rejoicing here, how you feel while you're speaking comes through, and with Strength that tends to be calm.

With a brother or sister, it can mean finally having an old conversation without it turning into the old argument. In learning, it's the patience to stick with something hard until it clicks. In your messages it's the reply that's shorter and kinder than your first draft. Before you send a difficult message, read it out loud once, slowly, and cut anything that sounds like you're trying to win.
3.reversed:
Flipped in the third house, your voice loses its warmth. Words come out sharp or scattered, you talk to win or to fill a silence, and the quick energy of the house runs to nervous chatter. Fire and air wind each other up, so small exchanges flare where they'd normally pass.

It shows in messages sent too fast and regretted, and in a sibling or neighbour who's become a running irritation. Arguments over tiny things, a parking space, a group chat, take up far more room in your head than they deserve. In learning, a restless mind won't settle long enough to take anything in. Sometimes it goes the other way and you swallow what you mean. Say less, say it slower, and hear the other person out before you answer.

4.upright:
The fourth house is home, the family you came from, and the private ground nobody else sees. It's angular, a corner of the chart, so what happens here matters. Its natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon, and Leo sits right beside Cancer, neighbours with little in common, each holding what the other lacks. Fire and water are opposed elements. So this card lands in the chart's most tender place carrying a lot of heat, and there'll be some steam.

What Strength brings home is backbone. The fourth house is protective, and the care there often happens out of sight. Leo's care is more visible, warm and a bit proud, the kind of strength that holds a household together through a hard stretch by being calm in front of everyone. You may find yourself becoming the steady one at home or in your family, and people leaning on it. The friction is that fire can feel loud in a watery house. Some of your family may find your confidence a bit much, especially if they remember you as someone younger and quieter.

With family, this can look like holding your ground with a parent without going cold or giving in. At home it's a place kept together by patience, the dinner cooked on a bad day, the argument calmed down. With your own history, it's the strength you got from where you came from, and deciding which parts of it you still want. Let someone at home look after you for once, and don't argue about it.
4.reversed:
Upside down in the fourth house, the warmth at home runs unevenly. Tempers flare behind closed doors, or you keep steadying everyone and nobody steadies you, and the place that should feel safe gets tense. Fire and water clash, and the home either heats up or goes very quiet.

You'll see it in a household held together by your effort alone, and in family dynamics where you get hard or withdraw. Roots can feel like a weight you're carrying. Old family patterns about who gets to be strong and who's allowed to fall apart can come back up, sometimes at a birthday or a funeral. Ask for the steadiness you keep giving, from the person at home most able to give it.

5.upright:
Leo's own house is the fifth, the house of play, the things you make for the joy of it, romance, children, parties, anything done for delight. The Sun is its natural ruler and Venus rejoices here. So Strength in the fifth is the card at home, Leo's Major in Leo's house, fire in its own element. There's nothing to reconcile. The house and the card want exactly the same things, and the card turns all of them up.

This is where Strength is most relaxed and most open-hearted. The fifth house wants you to make things boldly, love out loud, and treat joy as something worth being brave about, and the card backs every bit of that with warmth that lasts. Whatever you make or love from here has heart in it and tends to stick. The caution, with so much fire in one place, is showing off, the creative work made for the reaction, the romance played for an audience. If you keep it honest, the fifth is one of the happiest houses this card can land in.

In creative work, it's making the thing and actually finishing it. In romance, it's loving generously without needing to perform the evening. With children, your own or anyone else's, it's a warm, encouraging presence they'll remember. In play, it's letting yourself enjoy what you're good at without apologising for it. Make something you love, for no reason, and show it to one person.
5.reversed:
Reversed in its own house, the card's fire turns to performance. Creative work gets blocked by the need for it to be impressive, romance becomes a stage, and the delight the fifth house is built for gets lost under the pressure to shine. Doubled fire off balance either blazes into ego or gutters into a block that feels like the light's gone out.

It shows in work made for the reaction and not the love of it, and in romances run on flattery and drama. With children it can show as wanting them to be impressive. There can be a joylessness under all the show. Make something small with no audience in mind, a sketch, a meal, a song in the car, and don't show it to anyone.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the ordinary day, the routine, the job as you actually do it, and the body's upkeep, sleep and meals and the walk you keep meaning to take. It's cadent, a house of adjusting and serving. Its natural sign is Virgo, ruled by Mercury, and Mars has its joy here, which gives the house some drive. Leo sits beside Virgo, a neighbour with little in common, and fire and earth have to be introduced. So a big, warm card has to find its place in a modest house full of detail.

What Strength brings to the sixth is patience with the daily grind and gentleness toward the body. Left to itself this house can turn a routine into a regime and the body into a project to be corrected. Strength's heat is steadier than that. It renews itself, and it suits the long game of health far better than any crash effort. You'll feel the friction. Virgo's standards and Mars's drive want results, and Leo wants to enjoy the doing. Put together, they can make habits that actually last.

With the body, this is strength built from small, kind habits kept up, a walk most days beating a gym membership you dread. At work it's bringing warmth to the tasks nobody sees, and being decent to the people beside you. With routine, it's care that keeps you going. Pick one habit you've been forcing, make it easier, and keep doing the easier version.
6.reversed:
In the sixth house the reversed card turns the daily upkeep against you. Routine hardens into a regime, self-criticism runs the health choices, and the body gets driven or picked over when it needs looking after. With fire and earth not warming each other, there's no kindness in the effort, just the grind, and Mars, which rejoices in this house, can push you well past sensible.

It shows in overwork that drains you, in a fussy, anxious relationship with food, and in energy worn thin by harshness. At work it can show as resentment of a colleague who doesn't try as hard. Treat rest as part of the job. Drop one rule you've been keeping about food or exercise, and see whether anything bad actually happens.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite, a partner in love or in business, the close one-to-ones, the contracts. It's angular, a corner of the chart, so what happens here is visible and it counts. Libra is its natural sign and Venus its ruler, and Leo sits two signs from Libra, a sextile, with fire and air feeding each other. That makes it a friendly placement for the card, easy to use as long as you actually use it.

What Strength lends the seventh is a way to hold your own inside closeness. You meet a partner warmly and steadily, and you neither dominate them nor disappear into them. When they're in a bad mood, you can stay calm without it being a performance. When there's a rough patch, you're the one with patience left over. The sextile makes this come fairly naturally, and Venus, the house's ruler, likes things fair and pleasant, which suits Leo's generosity well.

In love, this is a bond held through a hard stretch by patience, a difficult mood met calmly, and generosity going both ways. In business it's a partnership where you hold your position warmly and the other person trusts you for it. With whoever you're closest to, it's staying soft and solid at once. When your partner is having a bad day, stay near them and be kind, and leave the fixing for later.
7.reversed:
Partnership loses its balance when Strength reverses in the seventh house. You either dominate the person opposite, needing to be the strong one, or you dissolve into them, giving so much that there's nobody left on your side of the relationship. The warmth that should steady the bond turns into force or fear.

You'll see it as resentment building under a pleasant surface, and in meeting a partner's moods with heat or with collapse. In business it can be a partnership where one of you is quietly carrying the other. It can be a contract you signed to be agreeable. Say one honest thing to your partner that you've been saving up, calmly, and listen to the whole of their answer.

8.upright:
Intimacy and sex, money you share with someone, debts and inheritances, and the big endings that change you all belong to the eighth house. Like the second, it's succedent, where things build up and get held. Scorpio is its natural sign, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, and Leo squares Scorpio, both fixed, which is friction that forces something. The elements fight too, fire against water. So Strength brings open warmth into the most guarded, powerful part of the chart, and the two press hard on each other.

What the card brings is warmth where this house usually keeps control. The eighth is where people guard hardest, and Strength asks you to go into intimacy, shared money and loss with a gentle kind of courage, without clamping down. She has both hands at the lion's jaw and there's nothing tense in her at all. The fixed square makes this real work. Fire wants to be open, water wants to hold on, and both are stubborn. It takes time, and it's worth doing.

In intimacy it's presence and warmth, in bed and out of it, and letting yourself be seen. With shared money it's steadiness and generosity where fear would normally grip, the joint account talked about calmly, the debt faced together. With endings and grief it's facing what's changing with quiet courage. Tell someone close to you one thing you've always kept back, and let them hold it.
8.reversed:
When the card reverses in the eighth house, the depths turn to control and holding back. Intimacy becomes a power game, closeness offered and pulled away, and shared money or old losses get held so tightly that trust suffers. Fire and water fight here, the warmth boiling off before it reaches anything, so you go colder exactly where you most want to be close.

It shows in a grudge kept for years, in closeness used as leverage, in fear around a debt or an inheritance. Grief that hasn't been allowed to move sits here too. A partner may feel they're never quite let all the way in. Loosen one grip. Say the vulnerable thing to the person it concerns, and let them a little further past the guard than usual.

9.upright:
The ninth house is the long view. Belief, meaning, study, travel, anything that makes your world bigger. It's cadent, a house of learning. Sagittarius is its natural sign and Jupiter its ruler, and the Sun has its joy here, which matters, because the Sun rules Leo. So Strength in the ninth is Leo's card in the house where Leo's own planet is happiest. Leo and Sagittarius are a trine, fire and fire, and it's a comfortable house for this card to land in.

What Strength gives the ninth is warmth and staying power in what you believe. This house reaches for meaning and can chase the next horizon forever. Strength steadies the search, so your convictions hold without needing to be loud. You'll probably notice people finding your optimism reassuring, and that you can hold a strong opinion and still listen properly to someone who disagrees. The risk with doubled fire is getting preachy, or being so sure you're right that you stop learning anything.

In study, it's the patience to stay with difficult material until it makes sense. In travel, it's meeting the unfamiliar with warmth and curiosity. With belief, whether that's faith or politics or a philosophy you live by, it's holding it warmly enough to include the questions. When you disagree with someone about something big, ask them how they came to believe it, and listen to the whole story.
9.reversed:
Reversed in the ninth house, belief either hardens or scatters. Conviction turns into something that won't sit with a single doubt, or it dissolves into restless meaning-hunting that never lands. Fire feeds fire with nothing to steady it.

It shows in a certainty that talks over people, in a faith too brittle to hold questions, or in chasing the next course, the next teacher, the next big idea. It can show in study dropped halfway, or a trip taken mainly to get away from something. With in-laws or people from a different background it can turn into arguments about how to live. Let yourself say 'I'm not sure' about one thing you've been certain of, out loud, to someone who'll take it seriously.

10.upright:
The tenth house is the top of the chart, your public role and reputation, the work you're known for and how people see your standing. It's angular, as visible as a house gets. Capricorn is its natural sign and Saturn its ruler, and Leo sits five signs from Capricorn, a quincunx, which means nothing much in common and a lot of small adjustment. Fire and earth need introducing too. So warmth has to find its footing in a serious house that cares about status.

What Strength brings to the tenth is authority through warmth. Whatever's here is on display, and with this card your public strength is the steady, generous kind, the manager who calms the room and earns loyalty without demanding it. The quincunx means it takes work. Saturn likes structure and results and doesn't always see the point of charm, and Leo can find Saturn's world a bit grey. They do go together with effort, and the result is a reputation for being both respected and liked, which is rarer than either.

In a career it looks like leading steadily and influencing without pushing. In reputation, it's being known as someone fair and warm who doesn't flap. With ambition, it's a climb that doesn't cost you your temper or your kindness. When you're in charge of something difficult, spend the first few minutes checking how people are before you talk about the problem.
10.reversed:
At the top of the chart, a reversed Strength makes public strength go wrong. Warm authority tips into a temper people see, or confidence wavers under scrutiny and you shrink from the standing you've earned. The quincunx pulls awkwardly, and your reputation ends up resting on force or on front.

It shows in leadership that dominates, and in a public face that cracks when it's tested. It shows in ambition chased so hard that the warmth drains out of it. A boss or a board may be pushing you, and you push back too hard or not at all. Ask one person who works with you what they'd like more of from you, and then do it, without making a speech about it.

11.upright:
Friends, networks, the groups you belong to and the hopes you have for later on all sit in the eleventh house. It's succedent, a house for building up. Aquarius is its natural sign, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, and Jupiter has its joy here, so there's generosity in this house. Leo is the sign opposite Aquarius, the same axis from the other end, and fire and air are friends. So the card's personal warmth meets the group-minded eleventh from across the chart, and the pull is toward balance.

What Strength brings to the eleventh is heart in the group. This house is about the many, and the card asks you to bring your own warm, personal courage into it, to be the steady one people gather round. The opposition is the useful bit. Leo's focus on the individual balances Aquarius's focus on everyone, so you neither disappear into the group nor keep it at arm's length. You'll probably find people coming to you, in the friend group or the club or the team, when things wobble.

With friends, it's being the one whose steadiness keeps a group together through a falling-out. In networks it's a generous presence that people trust and recommend. With your hopes, it's the nerve to aim at something big enough to include other people. Let one friend do something for you, and don't pay them back straight away.
11.reversed:
Your place in the circle feels off when Strength reverses in the eleventh house. You warm the whole group and go uncomforted yourself, or you hang on to your spot with effort, performing belonging while feeling outside it. The opposition pulls hard, and the personal and the collective won't balance.

It shows in being everyone's steady friend while nobody steadies you. It shows in friendships that take more than they give, and in hopes so tied to what a group thinks that you forget your own. A group chat can become a steady source of tension. Sometimes it runs the other way, and you stay on the edge of every group so nobody can leave you out. Tell one friend plainly that you've been finding things hard, and let them and the others look after you for once.

12.upright:
Nobody sees most of what happens in the twelfth house, sometimes including you. It's the house of retreat and solitude, sleep and dreams, and everything that works on you out of sight. Like the third, sixth and ninth, it's cadent, a place where things get processed and let go. Pisces is its natural sign, ruled by Jupiter with Neptune as the modern ruler, and Saturn takes its joy here, which gives some shape to the formless. Leo is a quincunx from Pisces, nothing much in common, and fire and water are opposed. So a card that likes being seen lands in the most private house there is.

What Strength brings to the twelfth is courage that works in the dark. This is the house of what's hidden even from you, and the card here is a warmth that keeps going with nobody watching. The awkwardness is real. Leo's instinct is to shine, and this house doesn't let anything shine in public. The gift is a strength that doesn't need an audience, which suits this house very well.

In sleep and dreams, it can show as rest that actually restores, and dreams that feel braver than your days. In retreat it's time alone that builds you up. With hidden things, fears, old hurts, things you've never said, it's the nerve to look at them gently. Spend some time properly alone, without a screen, and notice what comes up when nobody needs anything from you.
12.reversed:
Something strains out of sight when Strength reverses in the twelfth house. An anger you haven't admitted, or a fear you haven't said, works away under the calm you show people, and the warmth that should look after you in private can't get to it. Fire and water clash where you can't see them.

It shows in self-doubt you keep denying, in tiredness with no obvious cause, in sleep that's broken or full of anxious dreams. It shows in retreat that isolates when it should restore. Old habits of hiding how you feel can come back, the ones you thought you'd grown out of. Write down the thing you've been avoiding thinking about, somewhere private, and read it back gently, as if a friend had written it.
